p: The advent of generative algorithms has (1) _____ a fierce debate about the nature of creativity. Proponents argue that these tools merely (2) _____ human imagination, much as the camera once did for painting, while sceptics fear they will (3) _____ the very craft they imitate. History, however, suggests that technological disruption rarely (4) _____ art; it usually compels artists to (5) _____ their practice in unforeseen ways.

t: What should come in blank (1)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "The advent of generative algorithms has (1) _____ a fierce debate" (AI के आने से बहस 'भड़की/शुरू हुई'; precipitate = किसी घटना को अचानक जन्म देना)। बाकी विकल्प (quelled = दबाना, mitigated = कम करना) बहस 'शुरू' होने के अर्थ में फिट नहीं होते। Hindi Meaning: भड़काना / उत्पन्न करना.

t: What should come in blank (2)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Proponents' (समर्थक) कहते हैं कि tools सिर्फ़ मानवीय कल्पना को 'बढ़ाते' हैं, जैसे कैमरे ने पेंटिंग के लिए किया। Obliterate/Disparage/Impede सब नकारात्मक हैं, जबकि Proponents का पक्ष सकारात्मक है। Hindi Meaning: संवर्धन करना / बढ़ाना.

t: What should come in blank (3)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'while sceptics fear' – संशयवादी डरते हैं कि ये tools उसी कला को 'क्षीण' कर देंगे जिसकी वे नकल करते हैं। Erode = धीरे-धीरे नष्ट करना। Bolster/Cultivate/Venerate सकारात्मक अर्थ वाले हैं। Hindi Meaning: क्षरण करना / कमज़ोर करना.

t: What should come in blank (4)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'History, however, suggests... disruption rarely (4) _____ art; it usually compels artists to...' – 'however' के बाद विरोधी विचार आता है: तकनीक कला को कभी-कभार ही 'पूरी तरह मिटाती' है। Extols = प्रशंसा करना; Heralds = घोषणा करना; Replicates = नकल करना – कोई फिट नहीं। Hindi Meaning: पूर्ण विनाश करना.

t: What should come in blank (5)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'compels artists to (5) _____ their practice in unforeseen ways' – कलाकार अपनी शैली को नए, अप्रत्याशित ढंग से 'नया रूप' देते हैं। Relinquish (छोड़ देना) 'in unforeseen ways' के साथ अर्थपूर्ण नहीं है। Hindi Meaning: पुनः आविष्कार करना / नया रूप देना.

p: Behavioural economics emerged as a corrective to the neoclassical assumption that individuals are dispassionate maximisers of utility. Experiments by Kahneman and Tversky demonstrated that human judgement is systematically warped by heuristics: we overweight vivid but improbable risks, anchor on arbitrary numbers, and cling to the status quo even when alternatives are demonstrably superior. From this ferment arose 'nudge' theory, which holds that policymakers can steer citizens toward welfare-enhancing decisions without curtailing freedom of choice — for instance, by enrolling employees in pension schemes by default while permitting them to opt out. Enthusiasts herald nudges as a cost-effective alternative to coercive regulation. Critics, however, contend that the approach is paternalism in disguise: by exploiting the very cognitive flaws it purports to remedy, it manipulates rather than informs. Moreover, evidence from large-scale trials suggests that effects measured in laboratories often attenuate sharply in the real world, raising doubts about whether nudges can substitute for structural reform. The more defensible position is perhaps a modest one: nudges are useful supplements, not panaceas, and their legitimacy depends on transparency about who is nudging, and toward what end.

t: Which of the following best expresses the central argument of the passage?
o: Nudges have decisively replaced coercive regulation in all economies.
Nudges are a valuable but limited tool whose legitimacy requires transparency.
Behavioural economics has been entirely discredited by field trials.
Human beings are, in fact, dispassionate maximisers of utility.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: अंतिम वाक्य में लेखक का निष्कर्ष है: nudges "useful supplements, not panaceas" हैं और उनकी वैधता 'पारदर्शिता' पर निर्भर है। यही पूरे पैसेज का सार है; बाकी विकल्प अतिशयोक्ति (extreme) हैं।

t: The word "dispassionate" most nearly means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Dis-passionate = जिसमें भावनाएँ/जुनून न हो, यानी 'भावनाओं से परे, निष्पक्ष'। Neoclassical मॉडल मानता है कि लोग भावनाओं के बिना तर्कसंगत गणना करते हैं।

t: According to the passage, critics call nudging "paternalism in disguise" because it:
o: is far costlier than coercive regulation
exploits cognitive biases instead of genuinely informing people
has been rejected by most employees
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "by exploiting the very cognitive flaws it purports to remedy, it manipulates rather than informs"। यानी आलोचकों के अनुसार यह लोगों को सूचित नहीं, बल्कि उनकी मानसिक कमज़ोरियों से हेरफेर करता है।

t: The word "attenuate" as used in the passage is closest in meaning to:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'effects measured in laboratories often attenuate sharply in the real world' – प्रयोगशाला के प्रभाव असली दुनिया में 'कमज़ोर' पड़ जाते हैं। Attenuate = पतला/कमज़ोर करना। Intensify इसका विलोम है।

t: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
o: The author believes nudges should not be treated as a stand-alone solution to structural problems.
Default pension enrolment removes the employee's right to opt out.
Laboratory findings guarantee identical real-world outcomes.
Kahneman and Tversky endorsed coercive regulation.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक कहता है कि nudges "supplements, not panaceas" हैं और trials से संदेह है कि वे "structural reform" की जगह ले सकते हैं। इसलिए (a) अनुमान से सही है। विकल्प 2 पैसेज के विपरीत है (opt-out की अनुमति है)।

p: Beneath the abyssal plains of the Pacific lie trillions of polymetallic nodules — potato-sized concretions rich in nickel, cobalt and manganese, metals indispensable to the batteries that underpin the energy transition. Proponents of deep-sea mining argue that harvesting them would relieve pressure on terrestrial mines, many of which entail grievous human and ecological costs. Marine scientists counter that the abyss is no barren wasteland. Nodules themselves provide the only hard substrate for many organisms, and the sediment plumes generated by collection could smother life over areas far exceeding the mined zone. Since these ecosystems recover over timescales measured in millennia, damage inflicted today would be, for all practical purposes, irreversible. Regulators confront a dilemma of knowledge: the Authority governing the seabed must decide whether to permit extraction before the baseline biodiversity has even been catalogued. A growing number of nations urge a precautionary moratorium until the science matures, whereas others insist that delay merely entrenches dependence on environmentally ruinous land-based extraction. Both camps, notably, invoke sustainability to justify opposite conclusions.

t: What is the author's tone in the passage?
o: apathetic and detached from the issue
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक दोनों पक्षों (proponents और marine scientists) के तर्क रखता है और किसी का पक्ष नहीं लेता, इसलिए tone 'संतुलित और विश्लेषणात्मक' है।

t: The word "concretions" in the passage refers to:
o: hardened masses formed by accumulation of material
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Concretion = खनिज कणों के जमने से बना कठोर पिंड। पैसेज में इन्हें "potato-sized" nodules कहा गया है।

t: Why does the author describe the damage as irreversible "for all practical purposes"?
o: Recovery of these ecosystems would take thousands of years.
Mining has been permanently banned worldwide.
Nodules regenerate within a few years.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "ecosystems recover over timescales measured in millennia" – यानी हज़ारों साल लगेंगे, इसलिए व्यावहारिक रूप से नुकसान स्थायी है।

t: The "dilemma of knowledge" faced by regulators refers to the problem of:
o: disagreement over the chemical composition of nodules
lack of funds for patrolling the seabed
technological inability to reach the abyssal plains
deciding on extraction before baseline biodiversity has been catalogued
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: वाक्य में ही स्पष्टीकरण है: regulators को अनुमति देनी है "before the baseline biodiversity has even been catalogued" – यानी पर्याप्त जानकारी के बिना निर्णय।

t: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage?
o: Both camps appeal to sustainability to justify their positions.
Deep-sea ecosystems regenerate within a few years of disturbance.
Sediment plumes may affect areas beyond the mined zone.
Some nations favour a precautionary moratorium.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज के अनुसार recovery में 'millennia' लगते हैं, 'कुछ वर्ष' नहीं। बाकी तीनों कथन पैसेज में सीधे मौजूद हैं।

pp: 1. The devastation wrought by recent cyclones has, however, revived appreciation for their protective role.
2. Mangroves, which thrive in the intertidal zones of tropical coasts, anchor shorelines with dense root systems.
3. Consequently, many coastal cities now invest in mangrove restoration as a low-cost buffer against storm surges.
4. Yet decades of conversion into shrimp farms have eliminated vast stretches of this natural barrier.
5. These roots dissipate wave energy, thereby shielding inland settlements from erosion.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Trick (General → Detail → Contrast → Conclusion): 2 विषय (mangroves) का परिचय देता है → 5 'These roots' से 2 की जड़ों को आगे बढ़ाता है → 4 'Yet' से विरोध (झींगा-पालन से विनाश) → 1 'however' से चक्रवातों के बाद महत्व का पुनः बोध → 3 'Consequently' से निष्कर्ष (बहाली में निवेश)। सही क्रम 2-5-4-1-3।

pp: 1. Scholars have, accordingly, mined these verses to reconstruct trade, social hierarchy and ethics.
2. The Sangam corpus, composed roughly two millennia ago, offers rare glimpses into the everyday life of ancient Tamilakam.
3. Such classification reveals a culture that deliberately separated the private from the civic.
4. Its poems are classified under two broad heads: akam, concerned with interior emotional life, and puram, which treats war, kingship and public virtue.
5. Yet the corpus survived only through palm-leaf manuscripts rediscovered in the nineteenth century.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 2 मुख्य विषय (Sangam corpus) देता है → 4 'Its poems' से उसका वर्गीकरण → 3 'Such classification' (4 का सीधा संदर्भ) → 1 'accordingly' से विद्वानों का उपयोग → 5 'Yet' से अंत में पांडुलिपियों के बचने का विरोधी तथ्य। सही क्रम 2-4-3-1-5।

pp: Economists warn
P: will accrue disproportionately to workers
Q: rather than compete with them
R: that the gains from automation
S: whose skills complement the new machines
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "Economists warn that the gains from automation will accrue disproportionately to workers whose skills complement the new machines rather than compete with them." 'warn' के बाद 'that' (R) आता है; 'workers' के बाद relative clause 'whose skills...' (S), फिर तुलना 'rather than...' (Q)।

pp: The bridge
P: despite repeated assurances
Q: which was inaugurated with great fanfare,
R: developed alarming cracks within months,
S: from the engineers about its structural soundness
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "The bridge, which was inaugurated with great fanfare, developed alarming cracks within months, despite repeated assurances from the engineers about its structural soundness." Subject (bridge) + relative clause (Q) + verb (R) + concessive phrase (P) + उसका पूरक (S)।

pp: S1: Every language is, at bottom, a sediment of its speakers' history.
A. Loanwords, in particular, function as fossils, preserving traces of trade, conquest and migration.
B. English, for instance, bristles with words from Norse, French, Latin and, more recently, Hindi and Arabic.
C. Their presence is a record of the contacts that shaped the community that speaks it.
D. No tongue develops in isolation, however insular its speakers may imagine themselves.
S6: To study etymology, then, is to read a people's autobiography in miniature.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: S1 के बाद D सामान्य कथन देता है (कोई भाषा अकेली विकसित नहीं होती) → A 'Loanwords' उसका विशिष्ट रूप → B 'English, for instance' उदाहरण → C 'Their presence' (B के शब्दों का संदर्भ) → S6 निष्कर्ष। सही क्रम DABC।

pp: S1: The Indian monsoon is often described as the country's true finance minister.
A. A deficient season depresses rural incomes, dampens demand for consumer goods and, in severe cases, fuels food inflation.
B. Nearly half of the country's workforce still depends, directly or otherwise, on agriculture, which remains largely rain-fed.
C. Policymakers therefore track the progress of the rains with an anxiety that borders on the ritualistic.
D. This dependence explains why the arrival of the rains moves not just farmers but also markets.
S6: Whether such vigilance can ever substitute for irrigation reform is a question the monsoon itself cannot answer.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: B बताता है कि लोग वर्षा-आधारित कृषि पर निर्भर हैं → D 'This dependence' (B का संदर्भ) → A कमज़ोर मानसून के असर → C 'therefore' से नीति-निर्माताओं की सतर्कता → S6 'such vigilance' (C का संदर्भ)। सही क्रम BDAC।

pp: 1. Not everyone welcomed the change, since some towns resented relinquishing their "own" noon.
2. In 1883 the railroads therefore imposed standard time zones, which Congress formally adopted only in 1918.
3. Before the 1880s, each American town set its clocks by the local position of the sun.
4. The railroads' solution, though administratively crude, nonetheless laid the foundation for today's global system of time zones.
5. This arrangement sufficed until trains began to traverse hundreds of miles a day, bewildering timetables.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 3 पुरानी स्थिति (सूर्य से समय) → 5 'This arrangement' (3 का संदर्भ) और रेलों से समस्या → 2 'therefore' से समाधान (standard time) → 1 बदलाव का विरोध → 4 अंतिम प्रभाव/निष्कर्ष। सही क्रम 3-5-2-1-4।

p: Central banks, long (1) _____ for their inscrutability, have in recent years embraced forward guidance, hoping that transparency will (2) _____ market volatility. Yet candour carries its own perils: an offhand remark can (3) _____ a speculative frenzy, and a (4) _____ of caution may be mistaken for incompetence. The governor's task is therefore to speak with enough clarity to reassure, but with enough (5) _____ to preserve flexibility.

t: What should come in blank (1)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "long (1) _____ for their inscrutability" – 'for' के साथ 'notorious for' (किसी बुरी/अप्रिय बात के लिए कुख्यात) का सही collocation बनता है। Deprived/Absolved/Bereft के साथ 'of' आता है, 'for' नहीं। Hindi Meaning: कुख्यात.

t: What should come in blank (2)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'hoping that transparency will (2) _____ market volatility' – पारदर्शिता से उम्मीद अस्थिरता को 'कम' करने की होती है। Exacerbate/Instigate अस्थिरता को बढ़ाएँगे, Condone = क्षमा करना। Hindi Meaning: कम करना / मंद करना.

t: What should come in blank (3)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Yet candour carries its own perils: an offhand remark can (3) _____ a speculative frenzy' – 'perils' (ख़तरे) के संदर्भ में एक लापरवाह टिप्पणी सट्टेबाज़ी का उन्माद 'भड़का' सकती है। Foment = उकसाना/भड़काना। Hindi Meaning: भड़काना.

t: What should come in blank (4)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'a (4) _____ of caution may be mistaken for incompetence' – ज़रूरत से 'ज़्यादा' सावधानी (surfeit = अधिकता) अक्षमता समझी जा सकती है। Paucity = कमी; Modicum = थोड़ी-सी मात्रा; Semblance = दिखावा – इन सबमें 'अत्यधिक' का भाव नहीं है। Hindi Meaning: अधिकता / अतिरेक.

t: What should come in blank (5)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'enough clarity to reassure, but with enough (5) _____ to preserve flexibility' – लचीलापन बचाने के लिए थोड़ी 'अस्पष्टता' (strategic ambiguity) चाहिए, जो clarity का विपरीत है। Alacrity = फुर्ती; Austerity = कठोर मितव्ययिता। Hindi Meaning: अस्पष्टता / दुविधा.

p: For much of the twentieth century, sleep was regarded as a period of neural quiescence, a mere interlude of repair between bouts of meaningful activity. Contemporary neuroscience has overturned this view. During slow-wave sleep, the hippocampus appears to 'replay' the day's experiences in compressed form, transferring them to the neocortex for long-term storage. Rapid-eye-movement sleep, by contrast, seems to prune and integrate these traces, which may explain why people often emerge from sleep with novel solutions to problems that stymied them the night before. Experiments reinforce the point: participants who slept after learning a task outperformed those who stayed awake for an equivalent period, even when the waking group was allowed to rehearse. Yet scientists caution against glib extrapolation. Correlation between sleep duration and cognitive performance does not establish that extra sleep will confer extra intelligence, and the mechanisms by which memories are 'selected' for consolidation remain murky. What is no longer defensible is the cultural glorification of sleeplessness as a badge of industriousness; the evidence suggests that those who forgo sleep are not gaining time but squandering the capacity to use it well.

t: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
o: Sleep is a passive interlude that matters little to cognition.
Longer sleep reliably makes people more intelligent.
Sleep is an active process essential to memory, so sacrificing it is counterproductive.
Rehearsal while awake is superior to sleep for learning.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज पुरानी सोच (sleep = निष्क्रिय) को खारिज करता है, memory consolidation में नींद की भूमिका बताता है और अंत में कहता है कि नींद त्यागना समय बचाना नहीं, बल्कि क्षमता गँवाना है। विकल्प 2 और 3 अतिशयोक्ति/विपरीत हैं।

t: The word "quiescence" most nearly means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Quiescence = शांत/निष्क्रिय अवस्था। पैसेज में पुरानी धारणा थी कि नींद 'neural quiescence' (मस्तिष्क की निष्क्रियता) है, जिसे आधुनिक neuroscience ने उलट दिया।

t: According to the passage, rapid-eye-movement (REM) sleep:
o: replays experiences in compressed form for transfer to the neocortex
stops the brain from selecting memories
reduces the effect of rehearsal on performance
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: slow-wave sleep में hippocampus अनुभवों को 'replay' करता है, जबकि REM sleep "seems to prune and integrate these traces"। विकल्प 2 slow-wave sleep का वर्णन है – यह एक आम जाल (trap) है।

t: The word "stymied" as used in the passage is closest in meaning to:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Stymie = किसी को आगे बढ़ने से रोकना/उलझा देना। 'problems that stymied them' = ऐसी समस्याएँ जिन्होंने उन्हें अटका दिया था; Thwarted = विफल किया/रोका।

t: Which of the following would the author most likely agree with?
o: Sleeping longer will necessarily make a person more intelligent.
The mechanisms of memory consolidation are now fully understood.
Prolonged wakefulness is not a dependable route to greater productivity.
Sleeplessness should be admired as evidence of industriousness.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक अंत में कहता है कि जो नींद छोड़ते हैं वे समय नहीं बचाते, बल्कि उसे अच्छे से इस्तेमाल करने की क्षमता गँवाते हैं। विकल्प 1 'correlation ≠ causation' के कारण, विकल्प 2 "remain murky" के कारण और विकल्प 4 "no longer defensible" के कारण ग़लत हैं।

p: Of the roughly seven thousand languages spoken today, linguists estimate that nearly half will fall silent by the end of the century. The usual explanation is economic: parents, perceiving that a dominant language offers access to schooling and employment, cease to transmit their mother tongue to their children. But this account, while not false, is incomplete. Languages seldom perish through a single act of abandonment; they erode through a cascade of small renunciations — a school that forbids the vernacular, a broadcaster that ignores it, a bureaucracy that cannot process it. Each, taken alone, seems trivial; together, they sever the intergenerational thread. The loss is not merely sentimental. Each language encodes a distinctive taxonomy of the natural world, a repository of ecological and medicinal knowledge accumulated over centuries, and when the last fluent speaker dies, that knowledge usually dies with them. Revitalisation efforts, such as immersion nurseries for Māori and Hawaiian, show that decline is not destiny, but they demand sustained institutional commitment rather than mere nostalgia.

t: The author's attitude toward the "economic explanation" for language loss is best described as:
o: partially accepting but finding it incomplete
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक कहता है: "this account, while not false, is incomplete" – यानी वह इसे आंशिक रूप से सही मानता है, पर पूर्ण नहीं।

t: The phrase "cascade of small renunciations" most nearly suggests:
o: a chain of minor acts of abandonment that accumulate into major loss
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Cascade = एक के बाद एक आने वाली श्रृंखला; renunciation = त्याग। उदाहरण (स्कूल, प्रसारक, नौकरशाही) दिखाते हैं कि छोटे-छोटे त्याग मिलकर बड़ा नुकसान करते हैं।

t: The "intergenerational thread" in the passage refers to:
o: the transmission of a language from one generation to the next
the genetic similarity between old and young speakers
a government scheme linking schools and elders
the grammatical structure shared by all languages
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पिछले वाक्यों में माता-पिता का अपनी मातृभाषा को बच्चों को न सौंपना बताया गया है। 'Thread' वही कड़ी है जो पीढ़ी-दर-पीढ़ी भाषा को जोड़ती है।

t: What does the author imply by "decline is not destiny"?
o: All endangered languages will inevitably be revived.
Language decline has no real causes.
Language loss can be reversed through sustained effort.
Nostalgia alone is enough to save a language.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Māori और Hawaiian के उदाहरण दिखाते हैं कि गिरावट अपरिहार्य नहीं है – पर साथ ही लेखक कहता है कि इसके लिए 'sustained institutional commitment' चाहिए, 'mere nostalgia' नहीं। इसलिए विकल्प 2 और 4 अति-सरलीकरण हैं।

t: Which of the following would be the most appropriate title for the passage?
o: The Economics of Schooling in Rural Areas
Silent Tongues: Why Languages Die and Whether They Can Live Again
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज भाषाओं के लुप्त होने के कारण, उसके नुकसान और पुनर्जीवन की संभावना – तीनों पर बात करता है; यही शीर्षक पूरी सामग्री को समेटता है।

pp: 1. The Church, for instance, found its authority over scriptural interpretation challenged by vernacular Bibles.
2. This democratisation of knowledge unsettled institutions that had long monopolised literacy.
3. Literacy rates, though initially modest, climbed steadily over the following centuries.
4. The printing press, introduced to Europe by Gutenberg around 1450, made books affordable to an unprecedented number of readers.
5. Before the mid-fifteenth century, manuscripts were copied by hand, rendering them scarce and expensive.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 5 पुरानी स्थिति (हाथ से नक़ल) → 4 प्रिंटिंग प्रेस का आगमन → 2 'This democratisation' (4 का परिणाम) → 1 'for instance' से Church का उदाहरण (2 के institutions का) → 3 अंततः साक्षरता में वृद्धि। सही क्रम 5-4-2-1-3।

pp: 1. The dance, decoded by Karl von Frisch, conveys both the direction and the distance of a food source.
2. When a forager bee returns to the hive, it performs a figure-eight "waggle dance" on the comb.
3. Von Frisch's work earned him a Nobel Prize in 1973, a rare honour for a study of insect behaviour.
4. The angle of the central run, relative to the vertical, corresponds to the angle between the sun and the food.
5. The duration of the waggling, meanwhile, signals how far the nectar lies.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 2 नृत्य का परिचय देता है → 1 'The dance' (2 का संदर्भ) उसका कार्य बताता है → 4 दिशा का तरीका → 5 'meanwhile' से दूरी का तरीका (4 के बाद ही) → 3 अंत में Nobel Prize की जानकारी। सही क्रम 2-1-4-5-3।

pp: Despite its vast mineral wealth,
P: where infrastructure is scant
Q: one of the poorest in the country
R: the region remains
S: and literacy rates abysmal
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "Despite its vast mineral wealth, the region remains one of the poorest in the country, where infrastructure is scant and literacy rates abysmal." 'the region remains' (R) → 'one of the poorest...' (Q) → relative clause 'where...' (P) → 'and' से जुड़ा अंतिम अंश (S)।

pp: The scientist
P: was awarded the prize
Q: for decades,
R: who had been working in obscurity
S: for her pioneering research
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "The scientist, who had been working in obscurity for decades, was awarded the prize for her pioneering research." Non-defining clause 'who had been...' (R + Q) subject के ठीक बाद, फिर मुख्य क्रिया (P) और उसका कारण (S)।

pp: S1: Cities are not merely collections of buildings; they are arguments about how people ought to live together.
A. A wide boulevard, for example, announces ambitions of order and grandeur.
B. Every street plan, therefore, embodies a set of values, whether its planners acknowledge them or not.
C. A warren of narrow alleys, by contrast, records centuries of unplanned, organic accretion.
D. These values then shape, quietly but persistently, the habits of the residents who walk those streets.
S6: To change a city's design is, in the end, to renegotiate a society's understanding of itself.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: S1 के 'arguments about how to live' से B (street plan = values) जुड़ता है → A 'for example' (boulevard) → C 'by contrast' (alleys; A के बाद ही) → D 'These values' (सारे उदाहरणों के बाद का असर) → S6 निष्कर्ष। सही क्रम BACD।

pp: S1: The invention of the mechanical clock transformed the way medieval Europeans experienced time.
A. Monastic bells, once rung to summon monks to prayer, gave way to public clocks that summoned merchants to market.
B. Time thus ceased to be a rhythm received from nature and became a quantity to be measured, spent and saved.
C. Until then, hours had been elastic, lengthening in summer and shrinking in winter with the sun's course.
D. Merchants, in particular, welcomed the public clocks, since wages and deadlines demanded precision.
S6: The modern obsession with efficiency may well be traced to that quiet revolution in the town square.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: C 'Until then' पुरानी स्थिति बताता है → A घंटियों से सार्वजनिक घड़ियों में बदलाव → D 'public clocks' (A में आया) का व्यापारियों के लिए लाभ → B 'thus' से निष्कर्ष (समय अब मापने की वस्तु) → S6। D, A से पहले नहीं आ सकता क्योंकि 'public clocks' पहले A में परिचित होता है।

pp: 1. Without it, neither modern algebra nor digital computing would be conceivable.
2. Zero began not as a number but as a mere placeholder, a blank that kept digits in their proper columns.
3. Through Arab scholars, the concept travelled westward and eventually transformed European commerce.
4. The Indian mathematician Brahmagupta, in the seventh century, was among the first to formalise rules for arithmetic with zero.
5. Treating the placeholder as a quantity in its own right was a conceptual leap of immense consequence.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 2 शून्य के placeholder रूप से शुरुआत → 5 'the placeholder' (2 का संदर्भ) को संख्या मानने की छलांग → 4 Brahmagupta के नियम (इस छलांग का उदाहरण) → 3 अरब विद्वानों के ज़रिए पश्चिम में प्रसार (काल-क्रम में बाद) → 1 'Without it' (zero) अंतिम महत्व। सही क्रम 2-5-4-3-1।

p: The demand for the restitution of looted artefacts has (1) _____ in recent decades, as former colonies, long (2) _____ by the loss of their heritage, press museums for answers. Curators, however, are (3) _____: many fear that returning one object will (4) _____ a flood of claims, emptying institutions that have (5) _____ the public for centuries.

t: What should come in blank (1)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'has (1) _____ in recent decades, as former colonies... press museums for answers' – उपनिवेश रहे देश दबाव डाल रहे हैं, यानी माँग ने 'ज़ोर पकड़ा' (gained traction)। Dwindled/Abated = घटना, Capitulated = हार मानना – संदर्भ के विपरीत। Hindi Meaning: ज़ोर पकड़ना.

t: What should come in blank (2)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'long (2) _____ by the loss of their heritage' – अपनी विरासत खोने से वे लंबे समय से 'आहत/दुःखी' हैं। Aggrieved = जिसके साथ अन्याय हुआ हो। Elated (प्रसन्न) और Emboldened (साहसी बनाना) तर्कसंगत नहीं हैं। Hindi Meaning: आहत / पीड़ित.

t: What should come in blank (3)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Curators, however, are (3) _____: many fear...' – 'however' विरोध दर्शाता है और कोलन के बाद 'many fear' (कई डरते हैं) आता है, यानी वे दुविधा में हैं। Ambivalent = दुविधाग्रस्त। Unanimous (सर्वसम्मत) और Jubilant (उल्लसित) संदर्भ के विपरीत हैं। Hindi Meaning: दुविधाग्रस्त.

t: What should come in blank (4)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'returning one object will (4) _____ a flood of claims' – एक वस्तु लौटाने से दावों की बाढ़ 'छूट पड़ेगी' (unleash = खोल देना)। Forestall/Deter = रोकना, Appease = शांत करना – इनसे 'flood' की भावना उल्टी हो जाती है। Hindi Meaning: बेलगाम छोड़ देना.

t: What should come in blank (5)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'institutions that have (5) _____ the public for centuries' – संग्रहालय सदियों से जनता को 'शिक्षित/ज्ञानवर्धित' करते आए हैं। Edify = नैतिक/बौद्धिक रूप से उन्नत करना। Bewildered/Rebuffed/Taxed संग्रहालय की भूमिका से मेल नहीं खाते। Hindi Meaning: ज्ञानवर्धन करना.

p: Privacy is commonly defended as a shield for the individual who has something to hide, an argument that invites the glib rejoinder: if you have nothing to hide, you have nothing to fear. This rejoinder, however, rests on a conceptual confusion. Privacy is not secrecy; it is the condition under which people may experiment with identities, entertain unorthodox opinions and err without permanent record. A society in which every utterance is archived and every movement logged is not merely more transparent; it is more conformist, since individuals, knowing themselves observed, tend to self-censor. Moreover, data aggregated from innocuous fragments can reveal what no single fragment would: a person's creditworthiness, health or politics may be inferred from patterns of purchases. The danger, then, is less that a malevolent official will read one's private letters than that opaque algorithms will quietly sort citizens into categories that determine their opportunities. Defending privacy is therefore not a luxury of the guilty but a precondition of an open society, in which dissent can ripen before it is declared.

t: According to the author, the argument "if you have nothing to hide, you have nothing to fear" fails because it:
o: overestimates the cost of data storage
assumes that officials are always benevolent
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "This rejoinder, however, rests on a conceptual confusion. Privacy is not secrecy"। लेखक के अनुसार privacy का मतलब छिपाना नहीं, बल्कि प्रयोग करने और ग़लतियाँ करने की स्वतंत्रता है।

t: Why does the author describe a fully logged society as "more conformist"?
o: Citizens are legally required to follow identical rules.
People who know they are observed tend to censor themselves.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: वाक्य: "individuals, knowing themselves observed, tend to self-censor"। निगरानी का एहसास लोगों को खुलकर बोलने से रोकता है, इसलिए समाज 'conformist' (एकरूपी) बनता है।

t: The word "innocuous" in the passage most nearly means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Innocuous = जिससे नुकसान न हो, सामान्य/हानिरहित। 'innocuous fragments' यानी देखने में मामूली, हानिरहित डेटा के टुकड़े, जो मिलकर बहुत कुछ उजागर कर देते हैं।

t: According to the author, the real danger of data collection is that:
o: officials will read everyone's private letters
opaque algorithms may sort citizens into categories that shape their opportunities
people will stop buying goods online
companies will store too little information
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "The danger, then, is less that a malevolent official will read one's private letters than that opaque algorithms will quietly sort citizens..." 'less... than...' संरचना बताती है कि असली ख़तरा दूसरा है।

t: The phrase "dissent can ripen before it is declared" suggests that privacy:
o: encourages people to hide criminal intentions
makes dissent illegal until it is declared
guarantees that all dissent will succeed
allows unconventional ideas to mature before they are publicly expressed
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Ripen' = परिपक्व होना। निजता लोगों को विचार को खुले में कहने से पहले पकने का समय देती है – यही 'open society' की पूर्व-शर्त बताई गई है।

p: The Green Revolution of the 1960s, which paired high-yielding seed varieties with chemical fertilisers and irrigation, rescued India from the spectre of famine. Yet its triumph was uneven. The new technology favoured farmers with capital and assured water, widening disparities between prosperous regions such as Punjab and rain-fed tracts elsewhere. Intensive cultivation of wheat and rice, underwritten by subsidised power and fertiliser, also drained aquifers and degraded soils, while crowding out pulses and coarse grains that were nutritionally richer and better adapted to arid conditions. Today, the very policies that once ensured food security have hardened into a trap: farmers are loath to shift crops because assured procurement guarantees returns for only a few commodities. Agronomists therefore argue that a second transformation is needed, one that rewards diversity and efficient water use rather than sheer volume. Such a shift, they concede, cannot be achieved by exhortation; it requires altering the incentives that make the status quo rational for each individual farmer, however irrational it is for the collective.

t: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
o: The Green Revolution was a complete failure from the start.
The Green Revolution solved a food crisis but left entrenched problems that now require a change of incentives.
Indian farmers should abandon wheat and rice at once.
Subsidies have uniformly benefited all regions equally.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज पहले Green Revolution की सफलता (अकाल से बचाव) बताता है, फिर असमानता, भूजल-ह्रास और 'trap' जैसी समस्याओं को, और अंत में incentives बदलने का सुझाव देता है।

t: The phrase "spectre of famine" refers to:
o: the haunting threat of widespread hunger
an actual famine that had already occurred
a government report on food prices
a ghost story about rural life
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Spectre = भूत/भयावह आशंका। 'rescued India from the spectre of famine' = भारत को अकाल की डरावनी आशंका से बचाया, यानी अकाल का ख़तरा बना हुआ था, आया नहीं था।

t: The statement that wheat and rice were "crowding out" pulses and coarse grains means that:
o: pulses and coarse grains were exported in greater quantity
wheat and rice were grown in smaller quantities
the expansion of wheat and rice displaced the cultivation of the other crops
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Crowd out = जगह/संसाधन छीनकर बाहर कर देना। गेहूँ-चावल की गहन खेती ने दालों और मोटे अनाज की जगह ले ली, जबकि वे पौष्टिक और शुष्क इलाकों के अनुकूल थे।

t: According to the passage, why are farmers reluctant to change crops?
o: The new crops require more irrigation than wheat and rice.
Government has banned the cultivation of pulses.
Assured procurement guarantees returns for only a few commodities.
Farmers are unaware of the aquifer depletion.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "farmers are loath to shift crops because assured procurement guarantees returns for only a few commodities"। ('loath' = अनिच्छुक)

t: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as a consequence of intensive cultivation?
o: Large-scale migration of farm labourers to cities
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज में aquifers का सूखना, मिट्टी का क्षरण और क्षेत्रीय असमानता का उल्लेख है, पर मज़दूरों के शहरों की ओर पलायन का कोई ज़िक्र नहीं है।

pp: 1. When water temperatures rise even marginally, corals expel the symbiotic algae that supply them with colour and nutrients.
2. Reefs, among the planet's most biodiverse ecosystems, depend on a delicate partnership between coral polyps and microscopic algae.
3. Deprived of them, the corals turn ghostly white and, if the stress persists, starve.
4. Repeated bleaching events leave reefs too little time to recover, endangering the fisheries and coastlines that depend on them.
5. Such bleaching, once rare, has become alarmingly frequent in a warming ocean.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 2 विषय (reefs और algae की साझेदारी) → 1 तापमान बढ़ने पर algae का निष्कासन → 3 'Deprived of them' (them = algae, 1 से सीधा जुड़ाव) → 5 'Such bleaching' (3 के रंग-हानि का नाम) बढ़ती आवृत्ति → 4 अंतिम दुष्परिणाम। सही क्रम 2-1-3-5-4।

pp: 1. He founded Santiniketan in 1901, an experimental school where classes were held beneath trees.
2. Rabindranath Tagore, though celebrated chiefly as a poet, harboured equally radical views on education.
3. Rote learning, he argued, deadened curiosity and severed the child from the living world.
4. The institution later grew into Visva-Bharati, conceived as a meeting place of cultures.
5. His remedy was an education in harmony with nature, art and the community.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 2 परिचय (Tagore) → 3 'Rote learning' की आलोचना → 5 'His remedy' (आलोचना का समाधान) → 1 'He founded Santiniketan' (समाधान का रूप) → 4 'The institution later grew...' (1 का आगे का विकास)। सही क्रम 2-3-5-1-4।

pp: Only when
P: did the government
Q: and announce relief measures
R: the monsoon failed twice in succession
S: acknowledge the severity of the crisis
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "Only when the monsoon failed twice in succession did the government acknowledge the severity of the crisis and announce relief measures." 'Only when' के बाद clause (R), फिर inversion (did the government – P), फिर क्रिया (S) और 'and' से जुड़ा अंतिम अंश (Q)।

pp: The novel,
P: a receptive audience
Q: though widely acclaimed abroad,
R: among its own readers
S: failed to find
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "The novel, though widely acclaimed abroad, failed to find a receptive audience among its own readers." Subject के बाद concessive phrase (Q), फिर क्रिया (S), object (P) और स्थान-सूचक अंश (R)।

pp: S1: The ethical status of animals has exercised philosophers since antiquity.
A. Bentham, however, shifted the question from reason to suffering: the issue is not whether they can reason, but whether they can suffer.
B. Descartes notoriously regarded animals as automata, mechanisms devoid of consciousness.
C. This reorientation made the capacity for pain, rather than intelligence, the measure of moral concern.
D. Such a view licensed practices that later generations would find indefensible.
S6: The debate, far from being settled, now extends to questions about artificial minds.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: B (Descartes का मत) → D 'Such a view' (B का संदर्भ) → A 'however' से Bentham का विरोधी नज़रिया → C 'This reorientation' (A के बदलाव का परिणाम) → S6। सही क्रम BDAC।

pp: S1: Few inventions have reshaped rural India as quietly as the mobile phone.
A. Fishermen, similarly, now consult weather forecasts before venturing out to sea.
B. Farmers, for instance, once dependent on middlemen for price information, can now compare mandi rates in real time.
C. These small shifts in information, multiplied across millions of users, amount to a significant redistribution of bargaining power.
D. The benefits, however, are not evenly distributed, for the digital divide still excludes many women and the elderly.
S6: Connectivity, in short, is a necessary but insufficient condition of inclusion.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: B 'for instance' पहला उदाहरण → A 'similarly' दूसरा उदाहरण → C 'These small shifts' (दोनों उदाहरणों का सार) → D 'however' से सीमा/असमानता → S6 निष्कर्ष। सही क्रम BACD।

pp: 1. Smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980, the only human disease to be so far eliminated.
2. The boy did not contract smallpox when later exposed, vindicating the hypothesis.
3. Edward Jenner noticed that milkmaids who had contracted cowpox seemed immune to smallpox.
4. Jenner's method, christened vaccination after the Latin word for cow, spread rapidly across the world.
5. In 1796 he tested his hunch by inoculating a boy with material from a cowpox lesion.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 3 अवलोकन (Jenner ने देखा) → 5 'he tested his hunch' (परीक्षण) → 2 परिणाम (बच्चे को स्मॉलपॉक्स नहीं हुआ) → 4 विधि का नामकरण और प्रसार → 1 अंततः 1980 में उन्मूलन। घटनाओं का काल-क्रम 3-5-2-4-1।

p: Scientific consensus is rarely the (1) _____ of a single experiment; it is the (2) _____ residue of countless attempts at refutation. Peer review, though often (3) _____ as an infallible gatekeeper, is better understood as a fallible filter, one that screens out the egregious but may (4) _____ the unorthodox. The system's strength lies not in its freedom from error but in its capacity for (5) _____ correction.

t: What should come in blank (1)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'consensus is rarely the (1) _____ of a single experiment' – सहमति किसी एक प्रयोग की 'परिणति/चरम बिंदु' (culmination) शायद ही होती है। Precursor/Prelude/Overture = पहले आने वाली चीज़ें, जो अर्थ उलट देती हैं। Hindi Meaning: परिणति / चरम.

t: What should come in blank (2)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'the (2) _____ residue of countless attempts at refutation' – अनगिनत प्रयासों से जमा हुआ अवशेष 'संचित' (cumulative) होगा। Ephemeral = क्षणिक; Fortuitous = संयोगवश; Cursory = सरसरी – 'countless attempts' के साथ बेमेल। Hindi Meaning: संचयी.

t: What should come in blank (3)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Peer review, though often (3) _____ as an infallible gatekeeper' – 'though' के बाद विरोध: अक्सर इसे अचूक द्वारपाल के रूप में 'बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर पेश' (tout) किया जाता है, जबकि यह 'fallible filter' है। Belittled का अर्थ तो उलटा है। Hindi Meaning: बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर प्रचारित करना.

t: What should come in blank (4)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'screens out the egregious but may (4) _____ the unorthodox' – 'but' से कमी बताई जा रही है: यह प्रक्रिया अपरंपरागत विचारों को 'दबा' भी सकती है। Embolden/Exalt सकारात्मक हैं, इसलिए 'but' के साथ नहीं बैठते। Hindi Meaning: दबाना / कुंठित करना.

t: What should come in blank (5)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'its capacity for (5) _____ correction' – व्यवस्था की ताक़त बार-बार दोहराई जाने वाली सुधार-प्रक्रिया (iterative) में है। Reluctant/Arbitrary/Fleeting 'capacity' के साथ सकारात्मक अर्थ नहीं देते। Hindi Meaning: बार-बार दोहराया जाने वाला.

p: Stoicism is routinely caricatured as a creed of emotional frigidity, an invitation to suppress feeling and endure misfortune with a stiff upper lip. This caricature misreads the tradition. The Stoics did not counsel the extirpation of emotion but the cultivation of judgement: what disturbs us, Epictetus observed, is not events themselves but our opinions about them. The distinction is subtle but consequential. A person who loses employment may legitimately feel loss; what Stoicism discourages is the further, unforced conclusion that life has thereby been rendered worthless. Its practical discipline lies in sorting the world into what is 'up to us' — our judgements, intentions and efforts — and what is not — reputation, health, outcomes. Critics object that this partition licenses political quietism, since it seems to counsel acceptance of injustice. Yet the Stoics, notably Marcus Aurelius, were men of public affairs who held that duty to the community was constitutive of a good life. Equanimity, on this view, is not an alternative to action but its precondition: one acts better when one acts without panic.

t: The primary purpose of the passage is to:
o: advocate the abandonment of emotions altogether
correct a widespread misconception about Stoicism
criticise Marcus Aurelius for political inaction
compare Stoicism with other ancient philosophies
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज की शुरुआत ही 'caricature' (भ्रामक छवि) से होती है और लेखक कहता है "This caricature misreads the tradition"; आगे पूरा तर्क उसी भ्रांति को सुधारने के लिए है।

t: The word "extirpation" as used in the passage most nearly means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Extirpate = जड़ से उखाड़ना/पूरी तरह मिटाना। लेखक कहता है Stoics भावनाओं को जड़ से मिटाने (extirpation) की नहीं, बल्कि विवेक (judgement) विकसित करने की सलाह देते थे।

t: According to Epictetus (as cited in the passage), what disturbs us is:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "what disturbs us, Epictetus observed, is not events themselves but our opinions about them"। 'not A but B' संरचना में सही उत्तर B है।

t: Critics claim that the Stoic partition of things 'up to us' and 'not up to us' may:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "this partition licenses political quietism, since it seems to counsel acceptance of injustice" – यानी अन्याय को चुपचाप स्वीकार करने की प्रवृत्ति।

t: How does the author respond to the charge of quietism?
o: By conceding that Stoicism is indifferent to society
By pointing out that Stoics engaged in public life and regarded equanimity as a precondition of effective action
By arguing that injustice does not exist
By claiming that emotions should be suppressed to avoid politics
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक का जवाब: Marcus Aurelius जैसे Stoics सार्वजनिक जीवन में सक्रिय थे और मानते थे कि समुदाय के प्रति कर्तव्य अच्छे जीवन का हिस्सा है; शांतचित्तता कर्म की 'precondition' है, विकल्प नहीं।

p: Planners have long treated the informal economy — street vendors, home-based workers, unregistered workshops — as an aberration to be eliminated through formalisation. Yet in many developing countries it employs the majority of the workforce, and its persistence cannot be dismissed as a failure of enforcement. Economists increasingly argue that informality is not a residue of backwardness but a rational response to the costs of compliance: registration, taxation and regulation are expensive, while the benefits of formal status, such as credit and legal protection, are often inaccessible to small enterprises in any case. Coercive formalisation, therefore, may merely destroy livelihoods without enlarging the tax base. A subtler strategy would reduce the costs of entering the formal sector and expand its rewards, thereby making formality attractive rather than compulsory. Whether governments possess the administrative capacity for such a calibrated approach is, however, doubtful; the temptation of crackdown, with its visible if short-lived results, remains strong.

t: What is the author's overall position on formalising the informal economy?
o: Informal enterprises should be shut down immediately
Informality is entirely a failure of enforcement
Incentive-based formalisation is preferable to coercion, though the state may lack the capacity to pursue it
Governments have ample capacity for calibrated policy
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक कहता है कि दबावपूर्ण formalisation से आजीविकाएँ नष्ट होंगी; बेहतर रास्ता लागत घटाना और लाभ बढ़ाना है, पर सरकार की प्रशासनिक क्षमता पर संदेह है।

t: The word "aberration" in the passage most nearly means:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Aberration = सामान्य से हटकर कोई विचलन/विसंगति। योजनाकार informal economy को ऐसी 'विसंगति' मानते थे जिसे ख़त्म करना ज़रूरी है।

t: According to the passage, coercive formalisation may fail because it:
o: may destroy livelihoods without enlarging the tax base
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "Coercive formalisation, therefore, may merely destroy livelihoods without enlarging the tax base." इसलिए विकल्प (d) सही है।

t: The phrase "visible if short-lived results" implies that crackdowns:
o: appear effective but do not last
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'visible' = साफ़ दिखने वाले, 'short-lived' = अल्पकालिक। यानी कार्रवाई तुरंत असरदार दिखती है पर टिकाऊ नहीं होती – यही उसका आकर्षण (temptation) है।

t: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
o: All informal workers earn more than formal workers.
Tax enforcement has fully succeeded in developing countries.
Small enterprises often gain little from registering, which weakens their incentive to formalise.
Formal status always grants easy access to credit.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: formal status के लाभ (credit, legal protection) "often inaccessible to small enterprises in any case" – इसलिए पंजीकरण का प्रोत्साहन कम है। यही अनुमान सही है।

pp: 1. Goods were not the only cargo; ideas, faiths and diseases travelled the same routes.
2. The Silk Road was never a single highway but a shifting web of caravan routes linking China to the Mediterranean.
3. Buddhism, for instance, reached East Asia largely through merchants and monks who followed these trade networks.
4. The Black Death, too, is widely believed to have spread westward along such arteries.
5. Few merchants travelled the entire length; goods typically passed through many hands, each adding a margin.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 2 मुख्य विषय → 5 व्यापार की प्रकृति (सामान कई हाथों से गुज़रा) → 1 'Goods were not the only cargo' (सामान से आगे की बात) → 3 'for instance' पहला उदाहरण (Buddhism) → 4 'too' दूसरा उदाहरण। 'too' हमेशा पहले उदाहरण के बाद आता है। सही क्रम 2-5-1-3-4।

pp: 1. The government's monopoly on salt, taxed heavily, burdened even the poorest households.
2. In March 1930, Gandhi set out from Sabarmati on a 240-mile march to the coastal village of Dandi.
3. On reaching the sea, he picked up a lump of natural salt, openly defying the law.
4. Thousands across the country soon followed his example, and mass arrests only amplified the movement.
5. Gandhi therefore chose salt as a symbol precisely because it was a necessity common to every Indian.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 1 पृष्ठभूमि (नमक पर कर) → 5 'therefore' (1 का कारण-परिणाम) प्रतीक चुनने की वजह → 2 यात्रा → 3 समुद्र पर क़ानून तोड़ना → 4 देशभर में अनुकरण। 'therefore' को 1 के तुरंत बाद आना है। सही क्रम 1-5-2-3-4।

pp: Not only did the company
P: expanded into three new markets
Q: surpass its annual targets
R: ahead of schedule
S: but it also
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "Not only did the company surpass its annual targets but it also expanded into three new markets ahead of schedule." 'Not only did... (Q) but it also (S)...' जोड़ी बनती है, फिर क्रिया (P) और क्रिया-विशेषण (R)।

pp: P: warns / Q: is likely to widen / R: submitted by the committee / S: that the budget deficit
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "The report submitted by the committee warns that the budget deficit is likely to widen." Subject (The report) + participial phrase (R) + verb (P) + noun clause 'that...' (S + Q)।

pp: S1: Translation is often dismissed as derivative labour, a mere carrying across of meaning from one language to another.
A. Indeed, a word's meaning is bound up with its sound, history and associations, none of which survive the journey intact.
B. The translator must therefore choose what to sacrifice, and every choice is an interpretation.
C. This is why great translations are themselves acts of creation, not copies.
D. Poetry, however, reveals how misleading this view is, since rhythm and rhyme are inseparable from sense.
S6: Fidelity, in translation, is thus less a matter of mirroring than of recreating.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: D 'however' से S1 की धारणा को चुनौती (poetry) → A 'Indeed' उसी का सामान्य समर्थन → B 'therefore' (A का परिणाम) → C 'This is why' (B का निष्कर्ष) → S6 'thus'। सही क्रम DABC।

pp: S1: The discovery of penicillin is often narrated as a stroke of luck.
A. Fleming noticed that a mould contaminating one of his culture plates had cleared the bacteria around it.
B. Yet luck alone does not explain the discovery, for countless others had seen such contaminants and thrown them away.
C. What distinguished Fleming was a prepared mind, one alert enough to treat an irritation as a clue.
D. Even then, the compound remained a laboratory curiosity until Florey and Chain purified it a decade later.
S6: Serendipity, it seems, favours those who are ready to be surprised.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: A घटना का वर्णन → B 'Yet' (संयोग की धारणा का खंडन) → C 'What distinguished Fleming' (B का उत्तर) → D 'Even then' (बाद की सीमा) → S6 निष्कर्ष। सही क्रम ABCD।

pp: 1. The 73rd Amendment of 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions.
2. Mahatma Gandhi had envisioned the village republic as the foundation of Indian democracy.
3. Early experiments after independence, however, languished for want of funds and genuine devolution.
4. The Amendment also mandated reservation of seats for women, bringing lakhs into public life.
5. Together, these provisions converted an aspiration into an enforceable framework.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 2 आदर्श (गांधी का सपना) → 3 'however' से शुरुआती असफलता → 1 73वाँ संशोधन → 4 'also' (1 के बाद अतिरिक्त प्रावधान) → 5 'Together, these provisions' (1 और 4 दोनों का सार)। सही क्रम 2-3-1-4-5।

p: Diplomacy is often (1) _____ as the art of saying nothing eloquently, yet its finest practitioners know that strategic silence must be (2) _____ with precision. A communiqué that is too (3) _____ invites suspicion; one that is too explicit may (4) _____ a delicate negotiation. The seasoned envoy therefore cultivates a studied (5) _____, committing to nothing while appearing to concede much.

t: What should come in blank (1)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Diplomacy is often (1) _____ as the art of saying nothing eloquently' – 'as' के साथ 'caricatured as' (किसी रूप में हास्यास्पद ढंग से चित्रित) का प्रयोग बनता है। Shunned/Bequeathed/Ratified के साथ 'as' का यह अर्थ नहीं बनता। Hindi Meaning: व्यंग्यात्मक रूप से चित्रित करना.

t: What should come in blank (2)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'strategic silence must be (2) _____ with precision' – रणनीतिक चुप्पी को सटीकता से 'नाप-तौलकर तय' (calibrate) करना होता है। Abrogate = रद्द करना; Squander = बर्बाद करना; Bewilder = चकरा देना – 'precision' के साथ अर्थहीन। Hindi Meaning: सटीक रूप से समायोजित करना.

t: What should come in blank (3)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'too (3) _____ invites suspicion; one that is too explicit may...' – 'too explicit' के विपरीत यहाँ 'बहुत अस्पष्ट' (opaque) संदेश संदेह जगाता है। Lucid/Candid/Transparent सब 'स्पष्ट' के पर्याय हैं, इसलिए विरोध नहीं बनता। Hindi Meaning: अस्पष्ट / धुंधला.

t: What should come in blank (4)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'one that is too explicit may (4) _____ a delicate negotiation' – ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा स्पष्टता नाज़ुक वार्ता को 'ख़तरे में डाल' सकती है। Consolidate/Expedite/Vindicate सकारात्मक हैं और 'perils' के प्रसंग से मेल नहीं खाते। Hindi Meaning: ख़तरे में डालना.

t: What should come in blank (5)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'committing to nothing while appearing to concede much' – कुछ न मानते हुए बहुत कुछ मानने का आभास देना 'equivocation' (दोहरे अर्थ वाली टालमटोल) है। Candour (स्पष्टवादिता) और Rigidity (कठोरता) इसके विपरीत हैं। Hindi Meaning: टालमटोल / द्वि-अर्थी कथन.

p: Money, in the end, is a social technology of trust. Coins, banknotes and bank deposits function not because of any intrinsic worth but because participants expect others to accept them in exchange. Conventional systems vest this trust in institutions: central banks guarantee currency, and intermediaries validate transactions. Cryptocurrencies propose a radical substitution — trust in code and consensus replacing trust in institutions — through a distributed ledger whose entries cannot be altered retrospectively without the collusion of a majority of participants. The ingenuity of the design is undeniable. Yet it would be premature to conclude that institutions have been rendered redundant. Price volatility undermines the unit-of-account function of such assets, the energy consumed by validation raises environmental costs, and, crucially, the cryptographic guarantee covers only the ledger, not the surrounding ecosystem of exchanges and custodians where fraud and failure have proliferated. Trust, it appears, has not been eliminated but merely displaced to new intermediaries, many of them less accountable than those they were meant to supplant.

t: Which of the following best captures the central argument of the passage?
o: Cryptocurrencies have made central banks entirely obsolete.
Money derives value from its intrinsic worth.
Cryptocurrencies have displaced rather than eliminated trust, often towards less accountable intermediaries.
Distributed ledgers are inherently incapable of securing transactions.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: अंतिम वाक्य: "Trust... has not been eliminated but merely displaced to new intermediaries, many of them less accountable" – यही पूरे पैसेज का निचोड़ है। बाकी विकल्प अतिवादी या पैसेज के विरुद्ध हैं।

t: In the passage, the phrase "vest this trust in institutions" means:
o: place this trust in the care of institutions
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Vest (in) = किसी को अधिकार/ज़िम्मेदारी सौंपना। पारंपरिक प्रणालियाँ विश्वास की ज़िम्मेदारी संस्थाओं (central banks, intermediaries) को सौंपती हैं।

t: Why does price volatility matter, according to the passage?
o: It reduces the energy consumed by validation.
It makes ledger entries easy to alter.
It undermines the unit-of-account function of such assets.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "Price volatility undermines the unit-of-account function of such assets" – जब क़ीमत लगातार उछलती-गिरती है तो वह मूल्य मापने की इकाई के रूप में काम नहीं कर पाती।

t: The word "supplant" as used in the passage is closest in meaning to:
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Supplant = किसी को हटाकर उसकी जगह लेना। 'the intermediaries they were meant to supplant' = वे मध्यस्थ जिनकी जगह लेने का इरादा था।

t: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
o: Exchanges and custodians are free of fraud.
Ledger entries can be changed by any single participant.
The cryptographic guarantee does not protect users from the failure of exchanges and custodians.
Central banks no longer guarantee any currency.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "the cryptographic guarantee covers only the ledger, not the surrounding ecosystem of exchanges and custodians where fraud and failure have proliferated" – इसलिए (c) सही अनुमान है।

p: For much of the nineteenth century, colonial historiography rendered the subcontinent's past as a chronicle of dynasties, replete with despots and decline, against which British rule appeared as an orderly corrective. Nationalist historians contested this portrait, but frequently by inversion, retrieving a glorious antiquity to set against imperial denigration. Both approaches, it has been argued, shared a premise: that history is the biography of states and elites. The Subaltern Studies collective, emerging in the 1980s, challenged this premise by turning attention to peasants, tribals and workers, whose resistance had been written out of both accounts or reduced to spontaneous 'unrest'. The project was not without its own tensions: recovering the voice of those who left few written records requires reading official archives against the grain, and critics wonder whether the 'subaltern' can ever be heard on his own terms or only through the interpretive mediation of the historian. Nevertheless, the enterprise enlarged the very definition of what counts as historical evidence.

t: The phrase "by inversion" in the passage suggests that nationalist historians:
o: reversed the colonial narrative by glorifying the past instead of denigrating it
accepted the colonial narrative without change
focused exclusively on peasants and workers
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Inversion' = उलटाव। उपनिवेशी लेखन ने अतीत को पतन बताया, तो राष्ट्रवादियों ने उसे 'glorious antiquity' के रूप में उलट कर दिखाया – ढाँचा वही रहा, केवल मूल्यांकन बदला।

t: According to the passage, what premise did both colonial and nationalist histories share?
o: History is essentially the biography of states and elites.
History should be written only by peasants.
British rule was an orderly corrective.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "Both approaches... shared a premise: that history is the biography of states and elites." Subaltern Studies ने इसी premise को चुनौती दी।

t: "Reading official archives against the grain" most nearly means:
o: accepting official records at face value
interpreting official records to uncover perspectives they were not designed to convey
reading archives in reverse chronological order
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Against the grain' = सामान्य रुझान के विपरीत। सरकारी अभिलेख शासकों की नज़र से लिखे गए हैं; इतिहासकार उन्हीं में से दबी आवाज़ें खोजने की कोशिश करते हैं।

t: The critics' doubt about the 'subaltern' is that:
o: the subaltern left too many written records
the subaltern is represented too accurately
the subaltern may be heard only through the historian's interpretive mediation
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "whether the 'subaltern' can ever be heard on his own terms or only through the interpretive mediation of the historian"। (mediation = बीच में व्याख्या की भूमिका)।

t: The author's evaluation of Subaltern Studies is best described as:
o: acknowledging its tensions while crediting it with broadening what counts as evidence
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Nevertheless, the enterprise enlarged the very definition of what counts as historical evidence' – लेखक कठिनाइयाँ स्वीकार करता है, पर योगदान की प्रशंसा भी करता है; इसलिए संतुलित मूल्यांकन।

pp: 1. When prices rise too quickly, central banks typically respond by raising interest rates.
2. Higher rates make borrowing costlier, cooling demand for goods and services.
3. The challenge lies in timing, for policy acts with long and variable lags.
4. Inflation, the sustained rise in the general price level, erodes the purchasing power of savings.
5. A premature tightening may choke growth, while a belated one may let inflation become entrenched.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 4 Inflation की परिभाषा → 1 'prices rise too quickly' पर ब्याज दर बढ़ाना → 2 'Higher rates' (1 का सीधा परिणाम) → 3 'The challenge lies in timing' → 5 timing की ग़लती के दोनों परिणाम। सही क्रम 4-1-2-3-5।

pp: 1. Many of these poets also questioned caste distinctions, insisting that devotion, not birth, determined worth.
2. The Bhakti saints of medieval India, such as Kabir and Mirabai, emphasised personal devotion over ritual orthodoxy.
3. Their verses, composed in vernacular tongues rather than Sanskrit, carried devotion to the doorstep of ordinary people.
4. Such accessibility unsettled the monopoly that priestly elites had enjoyed over sacred knowledge.
5. The movement's legacy survives in the songs still sung in homes and temples across the country.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 2 परिचय (Bhakti saints) → 3 'Their verses' (2 के संतों का संदर्भ) → 4 'Such accessibility' (3 की सुलभता) → 1 'also' से जाति-प्रश्न की अतिरिक्त बात → 5 विरासत (निष्कर्ष)। सही क्रम 2-3-4-1-5।

pp: Rarely does
P: appear
Q: in a single individual
R: talent and temperament
S: such a combination of
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "Rarely does such a combination of talent and temperament appear in a single individual." 'Rarely does' के बाद subject (S + R), फिर क्रिया (P), फिर स्थान/पात्र (Q)।

pp: P: Having failed to secure a majority / Q: the coalition government / R: in the lower house, / S: resigned
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "Having failed to secure a majority in the lower house, the coalition government resigned." Participial phrase (P + R) पहले, फिर subject (Q) और अंत में क्रिया (S)।

pp: S1: Memory is not a recording but a reconstruction.
A. Each act of recollection reassembles fragments, filling gaps with plausible inference.
B. Eyewitnesses, as a result, often recall details with complete confidence that later prove false.
C. This malleability is not a defect but the price of a mind flexible enough to imagine the future.
D. Experimental psychologists have demonstrated this vulnerability, showing that suggestion alone can implant entirely fictitious events.
S6: Courts are therefore increasingly cautious about treating confident recall as proof.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: A मूल कथन (reconstruction) → B 'as a result' (A का परिणाम) → D 'this vulnerability' (B की ग़लत-मगर-आत्मविश्वासी स्मृति) → C 'This malleability' (D में दिखी लचीलापन) → S6 'therefore'। सही क्रम ABDC।

pp: S1: The rise of remote work has unsettled long-standing assumptions about the geography of employment.
A. Companies once clustered in expensive metropolitan centres to draw upon deep pools of talent.
B. That logic weakens when a skilled engineer can contribute from a small town hundreds of miles away.
C. Smaller cities, in turn, are discovering an unexpected opportunity to attract residents priced out of the metropolis.
D. The consequences for urban real estate, however, remain uncertain and hotly debated.
S6: What is clear is that the office is no longer the default location of work.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: A पुरानी स्थिति → B 'That logic' (A का संदर्भ) कमज़ोर पड़ना → C 'in turn' (B का परिणाम) → D 'however' (अनिश्चितता) → S6। सही क्रम ABCD।

pp: 1. The movement's success inspired similar protests across the Himalayas and beyond, shaping India's environmental consciousness.
2. In 1973, villagers in Chamoli, led largely by women, embraced trees to prevent contractors from felling them.
3. For these communities, forests were not timber reserves but sources of fuel, fodder and water.
4. The Chipko movement arose in the Garhwal Himalayas as a response to commercial logging.
5. Their non-violent resistance forced the government to impose a ban on felling in the region.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 4 आंदोलन का परिचय → 3 'these communities' (4 के गढ़वाल के लोग) और जंगल का महत्व → 2 1973 की घटना → 5 'Their non-violent resistance' (2 का परिणाम) → 1 'The movement's success' (अंतिम प्रभाव)। सही क्रम 4-3-2-5-1।

p: India's digital payments revolution has (1) _____ the way ordinary people handle money. A decade ago, a vegetable vendor (2) _____ only cash; today he displays a QR code on his cart and receives payments (3) _____ seconds. The shift owes much to a public digital infrastructure that is open, interoperable and (4) _____ low-cost. Yet challenges remain, particularly in rural areas where connectivity is (5) _____ and digital literacy is limited. Experts argue that unless these gaps are bridged, the benefits will remain concentrated in cities.

t: What should come in blank (1)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "has (1) _____ the way..." – 'has' के बाद Present Perfect बनाने के लिए V3 चाहिए: has + transformed। Transform (V1), transforming (V-ing) और transformation (noun) यहाँ व्याकरण के हिसाब से ग़लत हैं। Hindi Meaning: बदल देना / रूपांतरित करना.

t: What should come in blank (2)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "A decade ago, a vegetable vendor (2) _____ only cash" – 'A decade ago' भूतकाल का संकेत है, इसलिए Past Simple 'accepted' (केवल नकद लेता था) सही है। बाकी विकल्प यहाँ वाक्य-रचना में फिट नहीं होते। Hindi Meaning: स्वीकार करना.

t: What should come in blank (3)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "receives payments (3) _____ seconds" – समय की सीमा बताने के लिए 'within' (कुछ ही सेकंड के भीतर) का प्रयोग होता है। At/On/Behind के साथ 'seconds' का अर्थपूर्ण संयोजन नहीं बनता। Hindi Meaning: के भीतर.

t: What should come in blank (4)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "open, interoperable and (4) _____ low-cost" – 'low-cost' (adjective) को modify करने के लिए Adverb चाहिए: remarkably (बेहद)। Remarkable (adjective) यहाँ ग़लत है क्योंकि adjective को adjective modify नहीं करता। Hindi Meaning: उल्लेखनीय रूप से.

t: What should come in blank (5)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "particularly in rural areas where connectivity is (5) _____ and digital literacy is limited" – 'is' के बाद विशेषण चाहिए जो 'Yet challenges remain' से मेल खाए: patchy = असमान/अधूरा। बाकी विकल्प अर्थहीन हैं। Hindi Meaning: असमान / कहीं-कहीं ही उपलब्ध.

p: Cities across the world are rediscovering the value of green spaces. Parks, community gardens and tree-lined streets were once treated as ornamental additions to urban planning, easily sacrificed when land became scarce. Recent research, however, paints a different picture. Residents living near green areas report lower stress levels, and neighbourhoods with abundant trees are measurably cooler during heatwaves, reducing both energy consumption and heat-related illness. Green spaces also encourage social interaction, as shared gardens bring together people who might otherwise never meet. Despite these benefits, municipal budgets for parks are frequently the first to be trimmed, since their returns are diffuse and difficult to quantify. Planners argue that this short-sightedness is costly: the money saved on maintenance is soon lost in higher healthcare bills and greater demand for air conditioning. A growing number of cities are therefore treating green infrastructure as essential rather than optional, integrating it into housing, transport and drainage plans from the outset.

t: Identify the tense and voice of the sentence: "Parks, community gardens and tree-lined streets were once treated as ornamental additions to urban planning..."
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: वाक्य में 'were treated' = was/were + V3 है, और Parks खुद काम नहीं कर रहे बल्कि उन पर काम हुआ – इसलिए यह Simple Past Tense का Passive Voice है। 'once' भूतकाल का संकेत देता है।

t: In the passage, the word "diffuse" is closest in meaning to:
o: spread out and hard to pin down
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "returns are diffuse and difficult to quantify" – Diffuse = फैला हुआ/बिखरा हुआ। पार्कों के फ़ायदे (स्वास्थ्य, ठंडक, मेलजोल) कई जगह बँटे हैं, इसलिए उन्हें गिनना कठिन है। Concentrated इसका विलोम है।

t: According to the passage, why are park budgets "frequently the first to be trimmed"?
o: Parks are expensive to build but cheap to maintain.
Residents refuse to use public gardens.
Their benefits are scattered and difficult to measure.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "municipal budgets for parks are frequently the first to be trimmed, since their returns are diffuse and difficult to quantify." 'since' कारण बताता है।

t: What grammatical function does the clause "who might otherwise never meet" serve in the sentence: "...shared gardens bring together people who might otherwise never meet"?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'who' एक relative pronoun है और clause 'people' की विशेषता बता रहा है (कैसे लोग? जो शायद कभी न मिलते)। इसलिए यह Adjective (Relative) Clause है, जो noun 'people' को modify करता है।

t: What is the tone of the passage?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक शोध-आधारित तथ्य रखता है (analytical) और अंत में हरित ढाँचे को 'essential' मानने की ओर पाठक को प्रेरित करता है (persuasive)। हास्य, उदासी या उदासीनता का कोई संकेत नहीं है।

p: The village had never been fond of the new road. For the old men who sat under the banyan every evening, it was a grey scar that carried away their sons to the cities and returned them, years later, as strangers with unfamiliar accents and unfamiliar ambitions. Kamala, whose own son had left at seventeen, would walk to its edge each dusk and watch the trucks go by, though she never admitted what she was waiting for. When the letter finally arrived, written in the careful hand of a schoolboy who has learned to be formal with those he loves, she did not open it at once. She placed it on the shelf beside the brass lamp and cooked dinner as usual, as if the delay itself were a kind of dignity, a refusal to let hope be seen hurrying.

t: How do the old men of the village regard the new road?
o: As a welcome source of prosperity
As a cause of loss, since it takes their sons away and returns them as strangers
As a proof of the government's generosity
As a harmless path used only by trucks
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज: "it was a grey scar that carried away their sons to the cities and returned them... as strangers"। यानी सड़क उनके लिए बेटों को दूर करने वाली 'चोट' है।

t: The phrase "a grey scar" used for the road is best interpreted as:
o: a symbol of damage and lasting loss inflicted on the village
a literal description of its colour only
a sign of the road's beauty
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Scar = घाव का निशान। यह एक रूपक (metaphor) है जो सड़क को गाँव पर लगी स्थायी चोट के रूप में दिखाता है; केवल रंग का वर्णन नहीं।

t: Why does Kamala not open the letter at once?
o: She is angry with her son.
She wishes to preserve her dignity by not appearing eager, even though she is hopeful.
She has already read it earlier.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज के अंतिम वाक्य में: "the delay itself were a kind of dignity, a refusal to let hope be seen hurrying" – वह अपनी उम्मीद को जल्दबाज़ी में दिखाना नहीं चाहती थी।

t: Which of the following best describes the tone of the passage?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: बेटे की प्रतीक्षा, शांत संवेदना और संयमित भाषा से पैसेज का स्वर उदास पर शांत और चिंतनशील (melancholic and reflective) है।

t: In the sentence "Kamala... would walk to its edge each dusk", the phrase "would walk" expresses:
o: a habitual action in the past
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'each dusk' (हर शाम) के साथ 'would + V1' भूतकाल की आदत/नियमित क्रिया दर्शाता है (used to walk)। यह भविष्य की भविष्यवाणी या अनुरोध नहीं है।

pp: 1. At the 1936 Berlin Olympics, he led India to a third consecutive gold medal.
2. Later, the Indian government chose his birthday, 29 August, to celebrate National Sports Day.
3. Born in Allahabad in 1905, Dhyan Chand joined the army as a young man, where he began playing hockey seriously.
4. His astonishing ball control led spectators to joke that his stick must contain a magnet.
5. India's highest sporting award was also named in his honour.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 3 जन्म और शुरुआत → 4 'His astonishing ball control' (खेल-कौशल) → 1 1936 ओलंपिक की उपलब्धि → 2 'Later' से बाद का सम्मान (जन्मदिन पर Sports Day) → 5 'also' से एक और सम्मान (खेल रत्न पुरस्कार)। सही क्रम 3-4-1-2-5।

pp: 1. Relieved, he bought a ticket and reached the city just in time.
2. Dejected, he sat on a bench and wondered whether the opportunity was lost for good.
3. Rohan had stayed up all night preparing for the interview and overslept the next morning.
4. Then a stranger told him that a special train would depart in half an hour.
5. By the time he rushed to the station, the train had already left.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: कहानी का काल-क्रम: 3 देर तक जागना और सो जाना → 5 'By the time he rushed' (ट्रेन छूट चुकी) → 2 'Dejected' (निराशा) → 4 'Then a stranger' (उम्मीद की किरण) → 1 'Relieved' (अंत)। सही क्रम 3-5-2-4-1।

pp: The students,
P: when the examination was postponed
Q: were disappointed
R: who had been preparing for months,
S: at the last moment
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "The students, who had been preparing for months, were disappointed when the examination was postponed at the last moment." Subject के बाद relative clause (R), फिर क्रिया (Q), फिर समय का clause (P) और 'at the last moment' (S)।

pp: The scheme,
P: to cover
Q: launched in 2015
R: all districts
S: has been extended
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: सही वाक्य: "The scheme, launched in 2015, has been extended to cover all districts." Subject के बाद participial phrase (Q), फिर क्रिया (S), फिर infinitive (P) और उसका object (R)।

pp: S1: The old clockmaker had not left his workshop in three days.
A. His neighbours, growing anxious, knocked repeatedly but received no reply.
B. At last, the door was forced open.
C. There, bent over a half-assembled watch, sat the clockmaker, who looked up, startled, and asked whether it was already morning.
D. Inside, the faint ticking of a hundred clocks was the only sound.
S6: They laughed with relief, for he had simply forgotten the world in his work.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: A पड़ोसियों का दरवाज़ा खटखटाना → B 'At last' दरवाज़ा तोड़ना → D 'Inside' अंदर की आवाज़ें → C 'There' (वहाँ बैठा घड़ीसाज़) → S6 राहत। सही क्रम ABDC।

pp: S1: Kalpana Chawla's journey from a small town in Haryana to outer space remains a source of inspiration.
A. Born in Karnal, she was fascinated by aeroplanes from childhood and often watched them from the rooftop.
B. Despite her father's initial reluctance, she pursued aeronautical engineering at Punjab Engineering College.
C. She later moved to the United States, where she earned advanced degrees and joined NASA.
D. In 1997, she became the first woman of Indian origin to fly in space.
S6: Her life shows that ambition, backed by perseverance, can overcome even the steepest obstacles.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: जीवन-क्रम: A बचपन का आकर्षण → B इंजीनियरिंग की पढ़ाई → C अमेरिका जाना और NASA से जुड़ना → D 1997 की अंतरिक्ष उड़ान → S6 निष्कर्ष। सही क्रम ABCD।

pp: 1. Environmentalists have therefore called for stricter limits on single-use plastics.
2. Much of this waste enters the sea through rivers carrying discarded packaging from inland cities.
3. These particles then travel up the food chain, eventually reaching human diets.
4. Plastic, valued for its durability, is now found in the deepest ocean trenches.
5. Larger debris breaks down over time into microplastics, which marine animals mistake for food.
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 4 विषय (प्लास्टिक समुद्र की गहराई तक) → 2 'this waste' का समुद्र में पहुँचना → 5 'Larger debris' का microplastics में टूटना → 3 'These particles' (5 के microplastics) खाद्य-श्रृंखला में → 1 'therefore' से समाधान। सही क्रम 4-2-5-3-1।

p: The National Education Policy emphasises (1) _____ learning over rote memorisation. Teachers, who were earlier (2) _____ to complete the syllabus, are now expected to nurture curiosity. Critics, however, point out that classrooms in many government schools are (3) _____ equipped and overcrowded, making such reforms difficult to (4) _____. Without adequate funding and training, even the most (5) _____ policy may fail to produce results.

t: What should come in blank (1)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "emphasises (1) _____ learning over rote memorisation" – 'learning' (noun) से पहले विशेषण चाहिए: experiential (अनुभव-आधारित)। Experience/experiences noun हैं, experiencing यहाँ अर्थ नहीं देता। Hindi Meaning: अनुभव-आधारित.

t: What should come in blank (2)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Teachers, who were earlier (2) _____ to complete the syllabus" – 'were' के बाद V3 चाहिए और अर्थ 'दबाव में डाले गए' होना चाहिए: pressured। बाकी विकल्प न तो V3 हैं और न ही संदर्भ में फिट होते हैं। Hindi Meaning: दबाव में डालना.

t: What should come in blank (3)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "are (3) _____ equipped" – 'equipped' (V3/adjective) को modify करने के लिए Adverb चाहिए: poorly (ख़राब ढंग से)। Poor विशेषण है और विशेषण को विशेषण modify नहीं करता। Hindi Meaning: ख़राब ढंग से.

t: What should come in blank (4)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "difficult to (4) _____" – 'to' के बाद Verb की मूल रूप (V1) आती है: to implement (लागू करना)। Implementation noun है; implemented/implementing रूप 'to' के बाद ग़लत हैं। Hindi Meaning: लागू करना.

t: What should come in blank (5)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "even the most (5) _____ policy" – 'the most' के बाद विशेषण और उसके बाद noun 'policy' आता है, इसलिए adjective 'ambitious' सही है। Ambition/ambitions noun हैं और ambitiously adverb है। Hindi Meaning: महत्वाकांक्षी.

p: Antibiotics transformed medicine in the twentieth century, turning once-fatal infections into routine ailments. Today, however, their effectiveness is under threat. Bacteria, subjected to repeated exposure, evolve defences that render drugs useless, and resistant strains are spreading faster than new antibiotics are being developed. The problem is aggravated by human behaviour: patients stop courses of treatment as soon as they feel better, doctors prescribe antibiotics for viral infections against which they are powerless, and farmers feed them routinely to livestock to promote growth. Each of these practices exerts selective pressure that favours the survivors.
